haiti-gang-crisis-2023-2025.summary: After the 2021 assassination of Jovenel Moïse, armed gangs led by Jimmy "Barbecue" Chérizier formed the Viv Ansanm coalition, stormed Haiti's prisons and forced Prime Minister Ariel Henry to resign in March 2024; by 2025 the coalition held about 80 percent of Port-au-Prince despite a Kenya-led, UN-authorized multinational police mission.
account: The UN Security Council authorized a Kenya-led Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission for Haiti on 2 October 2023 (Resolution 2699). On 29 February 2024, Haiti's two largest gang umbrellas, the G9 Family and Allies and G-Pèp, united as the Viv Ansanm coalition under spokesman Jimmy "Barbecue" Chérizier, a former police officer, and launched coordinated attacks on police stations, government buildings and the international airport.

On 2-3 March 2024, Viv Ansanm stormed Haiti's largest prisons at Croix-des-Bouquets and the National Penitentiary, freeing roughly 4,700 inmates, then seized the main airport to block Prime Minister Ariel Henry's return from abroad. Henry announced his resignation on 11 March 2024, and a nine-member Transitional Presidential Council was sworn in on 25 April 2024.

Kenya's first contingent of 400 police officers landed in Port-au-Prince on 25 June 2024 under the MSS mission, which was authorized for up to 2,500 personnel but had only about 991 actually deployed by June 2025. In October 2025 the UN Security Council adopted Resolution 2793, transforming the MSS into a Gang Suppression Force with an expanded mandate and authorization for up to 5,500 personnel. By then Viv Ansanm controlled an estimated 80 percent of metropolitan Port-au-Prince.

points: A class video addressed directly to the Haitian people ("the tribe of Levi") after Ariel Henry's resignation reads the gang takeover not as mere crime but as the fruit of Haiti's leaders taking bribes from oppressors instead of serving their own people, and answers it from Lamentations: Israel's deliverance is not in any nation's hands but in obedience to God's commandments.

dominican-mass-deportations-2024.summary: Under a policy set by President Luis Abinader's National Security and Defense Council to remove up to 10,000 undocumented Haitians a week, the Dominican Republic deported more than 276,000 people in 2024 and well over 100,000 more in 2025, including hundreds of pregnant and breastfeeding women, drawing UN condemnation.
account: The Dominican Republic's National Security and Defense Council, headed by President Luis Abinader, ordered immigration authorities to remove up to 10,000 undocumented Haitians per week. The country deported more than 276,000 people in 2024, including over 94,000 in the final three months of the year alone. Deportations continued to accelerate into 2025: more than 119,000 Haitians had been deported by mid-2025, a 71 percent increase over the same period in 2024, and reporting later in the year put the figure above 145,000 Haitians deported, with nearly 20,000 repatriated between April and May 2025 alone, the highest two-month total on record.

The United Nations publicly condemned the deportation of about 900 pregnant or breastfeeding Haitian women in a several-month span, with the Secretary-General's spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric calling the practice a violation of international standards. Human-rights organizations including Amnesty International characterized the campaign as racially targeted.

cuba-blackouts-and-us-fuel-blockade-2024.summary: From 2024 Cuba's failing power plants and fuel shortages brought repeated blackouts, including a total nationwide blackout from 18 October 2024; in February 2026 the United States began blocking oil tankers bound for Cuba, its first effective blockade since 1962, and by May 2026 Cuba said it had run out of oil and diesel.
account: Blackouts began in February 2024, affecting 45% of the country on 13 February; in March outages of up to 18 hours a day brought protests in Santiago de Cuba. From 18 October 2024 a total nationwide blackout followed the failure of the Antonio Guiteras power plant in Matanzas, the largest. Blackouts continued through 2025 and into 2026, attributed to fuel and spare-part shortages, failing plants and, by some, the U.S. embargo.

In February 2026 the United States began blocking oil tankers heading to Cuba, targeting companies such as Mexico's Pemex; The New York Times called it the first effective U.S. blockade of Cuba since the Missile Crisis. On 13 March 2026 Miguel Díaz-Canel confirmed talks with the United States over the blockade, which had left Cuba with crippling fuel shortages and widespread outages; Cuba released 51 political prisoners and, on 3 April, more than 2,000 prisoners. On 14 May 2026 Cuba's energy ministry warned that the country had run out of oil and diesel.

cdamm-entry-on-iuic-2026.summary: On August 30, 2026 the Critical Dictionary of Apocalyptic and Millenarian Movements published Michael T. Miller’s entry on Israel United in Christ, which calls it the most populous Black Hebrew Israelite group and charges its teaching with conspiracy theory, selective misreading and an expectation of race war.
account: The entry, by Michael T. Miller in the Critical Dictionary of Apocalyptic and Millenarian Movements (edited by James Crossley and Alastair Lockhart), was published on August 30, 2026. It describes IUIC as the most populous group of the Black Hebrew Israelite movement and the most successful One West camp, with an estimated 10,000 members, led by Bishop Nathanyel Ben Israel.

It records charges in its own words: that IUIC’s eschatology predicts “the imminent ‘awakening’ of the true Israelites, followed by a race war and the enslavement/destruction of all non-Israelites”; that the group is a purveyor of “conspiracy theory in religion,” almost “conspiracy theory as religion”; that its history rests on “wild speculation” like a pseudohistory; and that “selective and seemingly deliberate misreading is also common.” It notes that IUIC, One West and Bishop Nathanyel “have been repeatedly accused of hatred, antisemitism, homophobia, conspiracy theories, and various other prejudices.”

The entry also records IUIC’s answer and its work: that IUIC “vociferously refute” the hate-group designation, open many videos with “We are not a hate group,” citing Romans 12:18, and tell members to notify the authorities of any plot to cause harm, citing Leviticus 5:1 and Romans 13:1. It writes that IUIC brings “a radically new message of race consciousness and dignity,” motivates people to improve their lives and commit to family, and does waste cleanup, youth and crisis support and prison outreach.

answer.why: IUIC’s own answer, as the entry records it: “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” No race war is taught by those who read this.
Cited by IUIC, as the entry records, for reporting any plot to harm anyone.

“After the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets.” Read in the classes against the names cult and heresy.
“As concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.” The apostles’ teaching was spoken against everywhere; the classes read it of themselves.

The ungodly say of the righteous: “He professeth to have the knowledge of God… He is grievous unto us even to behold… We are esteemed of him as counterfeits.” The ring: a people who call themselves the children of the Lord are charged with fantasy.
“A proverb, and a byword, among all nations”: the curse names the people’s story being made a byword.

colombia-earthquake-2026.summary: On August 10, 2026 a magnitude 7.4–7.5 earthquake centred near San José del Palmar in Chocó struck western Colombia, killing at least 335 people, injuring more than 4,600 and leaving 111 missing.
account: The earthquake struck at 07:34 with its epicentre 20 km from San José del Palmar in the department of Chocó; it was felt across western and central Colombia and in Ecuador and Panama, and caused extensive damage in Cali, Pereira, Quibdó, Manizales, Armenia and Buenaventura. At least 335 people were killed, more than 4,600 injured and 111 left missing; at least 107 died in Pereira, and in Chocó at least 14 deaths and 119 injuries were recorded.
President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of national disaster and three days of mourning; the United States announced US$26.5 million in relief.

points: “Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees”: unrighteous laws against the people, for the destruction of the people and of the land. When they take the precious minerals out of the earth the tectonic plates move and earthquakes happen; the minerals are in the earth for a reason.

They turn aside the needy from judgment and take away the right of the poor of my people, the rightful owners of the land. Chocó, Colombia's most Afro-Colombian department, was at the epicentre and paid the price for generations of government neglect: the people affected are our people, the indigenous and the Afro-descendants, and they are not getting help.
teaching.quote: Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees.

source.title: ABYA YALA UNDER FIRE

scriptures.why: Woe to them that decree unrighteous decrees and take away the right from the poor: the laws and mining that strip the land, and the neglect of the people of Chocó.
